([[Las Vegas, Nevada]]) | college = [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] (2012–2013) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = 2013 | career_end = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *[[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first team ([[2012–13 Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball season|2013]]) *Co-Pac-12 Freshman of the Year (2013) *[[Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] (2012) *[[Mr. Basketball USA]] (2012) *[[Jordan Brand Classic]] co-MVP (2012) *[[McDonald's All-American Game]] MVP ([[2012 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2012]]) | stat1label = | stat1value = | stat2label = | stat2value = | stat3label = | stat3value = | letter = | bbr = }} '''Shabazz Nagee Muhammad''' (born November 13, 1992) is an American former [[college basketball]] player for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. In his first season in the [[Pacific-12 Conference]], he was named to the [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first team and voted co-Pac-12 Freshman of the Year. Muhammad went to [[Bishop Gorman High School]], where he was named [[Mr. Basketball USA]] and [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] in his senior year. He was one of the top rated college basketball recruits in the class of 2012. [[College Basketball on CBS|CBS college basketball]] analyst [[Greg Anthony]] called Muhammad a "once-in-a-generation talent."{{cite web|last=Prisbell|first=Eric|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2012/11/16/ncaa-reinstates-ucla-shabazz-muhammad/1710617/|title=NCAA reinstates Shabazz Muhammad|date=November 17, 2012|publisher=''[[USA Today]]''}} After one season at UCLA, he [[NBA draft declaration|declared]] he would enter the [[National Basketball Association Draft|National Basketball Association (NBA) Draft]]. ==Early life== Muhammad was born in [[Long Beach, California]] to Ron Holmes and Faye Muhammad. Holmes was a {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m|adj=on}} standout, four-year starting [[point guard]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball]] program in the 1980's. He went by names including Ronald Muhammad, Ron Shabazz and Rashad Muhammad, but settled on Ron Holmes after never finishing his religious conversion. His wife Faye was a point guard and [[Track and field|track]] star at [[Long Beach State]]. Shabazz Muhammad was the second of three children. His older sister [[Asia Muhammad|Asia]] became a professional tennis player, and younger brother Rashad played basketball in high school.{{cite news|last=Bensinger|first=Ken|title=NCAA to NBA millions: UCLA star’s father mapped out a dream|date=March 22, 2013|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/news/columnone/la-fi-shabazz-muhammad-inc-20130322-dto,0,3133186.htmlstory|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6H2O3uHet|archivedate=May 31, 2013|deadurl=no}}{{cite news| url=http://articles.latimes.com/2012/apr/12/sports/la-sp-0413-ucla-shabazz-buzz-20120413 | work=Los Angeles Times | first1=Ben | last1=Bolch | first2=Baxter | last2=Holmes | title=There's quite a buzz about Shabazz Muhammad | date=April 12, 2012}}{{cite web|title=Shabazz Muhammad's 'killer instinct' at play|url=http://articles.latimes.com/2013/jan/02/sports/la-sp-0103-ucla-shabazz-muhammad-20130103}} When Muhammad was six years old, he was diagnosed with [[Tourette syndrome]].http://dailybruin.com/2013/03/01/not-looking-back-shabazz-muhammad-overcomes-disorder-in-becoming-one-of-nations-best-players/ ==High school career== Muhammad attended high school in [[Las Vegas Valley]] in [[Nevada]] at [[Bishop Gorman High School]], a Catholic high school with a $12,000 annual tuition that possessed a competitive athletics program. He became one of the few freshman to make their varsity basketball team. In his junior year, Muhammad led Bishop Gorman averaging 25.1 points and 7.7 rebounds for the season.{{cite web|url=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/player?id=72514&_slug_=shabazz-muhammad&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2fplayer%3fid%3d72514%26_slug_%3dshabazz-muhammad |title=Shabazz Muhammad |publisher=ESPN.com |accessdate=2011-07-15}} Muhammad was also named the 2011 [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] for the state of [[Nevada]]. Muhammad was the 2011-12 high school diary keeper for [[SLAM Magazine]].{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2011/10/shabazz-muhammad-diary-no-1/|title=Shabazz Muhammad, Diary 1|accessdate=March 29, 2012|date=October 12, 2011|publisher=''[[SLAM Magazine|SLAMOnline.com]]''|author=}} Muhammad played in the [[2012 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2012 McDonald's All-American game]], where he led the West team to a 106-102 victory over the East team, and was named the MVP of the game with 21 points and 6 rebounds. Muhammad also participated in and won the 2012 Powerade Jam Fest Dunk Contest.{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/highschool/03/29/boys.mcdonalds.game/|title=Muhammad leads West to McDonald's win, grabs MVP award|accessdate=March 29, 2012|date=March 29, 2012|publisher=''[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]''|author=Stephen Boyle}} He was rated as the No. 2 player in the class of 2012 in the [[ESPNU]] 100,{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/recruiting/rankings |title=2012 College Basketball Recruiting Rankings - ESPNU 100 |publisher=espn.go.com |date= |accessdate=2011-07-15}} the No. 2 player by [[Scout.com]],{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2012 |title=Scout.com College Basketball Team Recruiting Prospects |publisher=Scouthoops.scout.com |date= |accessdate=2011-07-15}} and the No. 1 player by [[Rivals.com]].{{cite web|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2509;_ylt=AiI6gfIcQUepfUTytuUWMB3WO5B4 |title=The Rivals150 2012 Prospect Rankings |publisher=Rivalshoops.rivals.com |date= |accessdate=2010-07-15}} ==College career== Boasting scholarship offers from scores of basketball programs, Muhammad's final list of schools was [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]]. On April 11, 2012, Muhammad announced he would attend UCLA.{{cite news|title=Vegas basketball prep star Shabazz Muhammad picks UCLA over Kentucky, Duke|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/vegas-basketball-prep-star-shabazz-muhammad-picks-ucla-over-kentucky-duke/2012/04/11/gIQAdyDSBT_story.html |publisher=washingtonpost.com |accessdate=12 April 2012|deadurl=yes}} {{Dead link|date=June 2012|bot=RjwilmsiBot}}{{cite web|title=Shabazz Muhammad to UCLA|url=http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/story/_/id/7803515/shabazz-muhammad-no-2-overall-recruit-commits-ucla-bruins|publisher=espn.go.com|accessdate=12 April 2012}} Muhammad was declared ineligible to play hours prior to UCLA's [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13]] season opener against [[2012–13 Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball team|Indiana State]] due to alleged violations involving the NCAA's amateurism rules surrounding unofficial university visits.{{cite news|title=Shabazz Muhammad ruled ineligible for UCLA Bruins|url=http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/ncb/story/_/id/8612665/shabazz-muhammad-ruled-ineligible-ucla-bruins|publisher=espn.go.com|accessdate=9 November 2012}} The NCAA ruled he had received benefits for travel expenses and lodging from family friend Benjamin Lincoln, who had befriended Muhammad's father when Muhammad was in seventh grade, during unofficial visits to Duke and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{cite web|title=Race and the NCAA|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/20/opinion/nocera-race-and-the-ncaa.html?ref=joenocera&_r=0)}} After missing three games and an appeal by UCLA, he was reinstated, and his family was required to repay approximately $1,600.{{cite news|last=Yoon|first=Peter|title=Shabazz Muhammad eligible to play|date=November 16, 2012|work=ESPN.com|url=http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/ncb/story/_/id/8640531/shabazz-muhammad-ucla-bruins-reinstated-ncaa|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6CEJ5rqvC|archivedate=November 16, 2012|deadurl=no}} Days before his reinstatement, several media outlets reported the boyfriend of the NCAA’s lead investigator boasted publically that the NCAA would find him ineligible eight days after the investigation commenced.http://articles.latimes.com/2012/nov/14/sports/la-sp-1115-ucla-shabazz-ncaa-20121115 The NCAA subsequently fired the investigator that was involved in the case.http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8768719/college-sports-fires-lead-investigator-shabazz-muhammad-case-according-report Muhammad scored 15 points off the bench in his debut in a 78–70 loss to [[2012–13 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] in the semifinals of the [[Legends Classic (basketball tournament)|Legends Classic]].{{cite news|last=Spector|first=Jesse|title=UCLA vs. Georgetown: Shabazz Muhammad's debut ends in defeat|date=November 19, 2012|work=sportingnews.com|url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-11-19/ucla-bruins-vs-georgetown-hoyas-score-shabazz-muhammad-debut-jordan-adams-stats|archiveurl=|accessdate=November 20, 2012}} He became a starter in the next game against [[2012–13 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]], and he scored a game-high 21 points in a 60–56 win in the Classic's consolation game.{{cite news|last=Holmes|first=Baxter|title=Shabazz Muhammad shows he's a quick study as UCLA beats Georgia|date=November 21, 2012|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/basketball/la-sp-1121-ucla-georgia-20121121,0,1189838.story|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6CLim1Gfp|archivedate=November 21, 2012|deadurl=no}} Muhammad would then get a college-high 27 points, including a game-winning three pointer, in a 97-95 overtime victory against No. 7 [[2012–13 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]].{{cite news|title=Shabazz Muhammad's 3-pointer in OT gives UCLA a 97-94 upset of No. 7 Missouri|date=December 29, 2012|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=http://articles.washingtonpost.com/2012-12-29/sports/36072099_1_shabazz-muhammad-laurence-bowers-phil-pressey}} He scored a game-high 23 points in an 84–73 road win over No. 6 [[2012–13 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]].{{cite news|title=UCLA rides huge start to surprise No. 6 Arizona|date=January 24, 2013|work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330240012|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6DvqHYDhc|archivedate=January 25, 2013|deadurl=no}} Muhammad was named to the [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first team, and was voted the co-Pac-12 Freshman of the Year along with [[Jahii Carson]] of [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]].{{cite news|last=Yoon|first=Peter|title=Shabazz Muhammad, Larry Drew II named All Pac-12|date=March 11, 2013|work=ESPN.com|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13549/shabazz-muhammad-larry-drew-ii-named-all-pac-12|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6F32POGVT|archivedate=March 11, 2013|deadurl=no}} Muhammad finished the season averaging 17.9 points, 5.2 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 0.7 steals, and 0.1 blocks per game. He shot 44.3% from the floor and made 71.1% of his free throw shots.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/61732/shabazz-muhammad|title=Shabazz Muhammad ESPN Bio|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=May 17, 2013}} While his scoing ability was unquestionable, he was not the flashy offensive player that was expected upon his signing. Muhammad struggled in the postseason, shooting 39.7 percent (23-for-58) and averaging 15.3 points in four games. He was 0-for-10 on [[three-point field goal]]s. He was a weak defensive player during the season, though he did show improvement. On April 16, 2013, Muhammad [[NBA draft declaration|declared]] he would enter the [[2013 NBA Draft]].{{cite news|title=Shabazz Muhammad to turn pro|date=April 16, 2013|work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|url=http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/9178426/2013-nba-draft-shabazz-muhammad-one-done-ucla-bruins|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6FwMdnYqg|archivedate=April 17, 2013|deadurl=no}} While he began the season projected as a top-three draft pick, his stock fell to being viewed as a back-end [[lottery pick]].{{cite news|last=Yoon|first=Peter|title=With draft stock dropping, Muhammad decision is a no-brainer|date=April 16, 2013|work=ESPN.com|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13747/with-draft-stock-dropping-muhammad-decision-is-a-no-brainer|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6H2RBU29H|archivedate=May 31, 2013|deadurl=no}} ==Personal life== Muhammad's uncle, [[Stephone Paige]], played nine seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with 377 career [[Reception (American football)|receptions]]. His aunt, Robin Paige, was a four-year starter for [[Cal State Fullerton Titans|Cal State Fullerton]].{{cite news|last=Foster|first=Chris|title=Shabazz Muhammad looks to add to family history|date=April 12, 2012|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://articles.latimes.com/2012/apr/12/sports/la-sp-sn-shabazz-ucla-20120412|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6H2Sdk1k3|archivedate=May 31, 2013|deadurl=no}} On March 22, 2013, it was revealed in a report from the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' that Muhammad was actually born exactly one year earlier than his thought-to-be birthday of November 13, 1993.{{cite news |url=http://www.latimes.com/news/columnone/la-fi-shabazz-muhammad-inc-20130322-dto,0,3133186.htmlstory |title=NCAA to NBA millions: UCLA star’s father mapped out a dream |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=March 22, 2013 }} A copy of his birth certificate on file with the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health shows that he was born at [[Long Beach Memorial Medical Center]] exactly one year earlier, making him 20 years old. ''Los Angeles Times'' assumes that this was to make Muhammed look better "competing against younger, smaller athletes, particularly in the fast-growing years of early adolescence", and compared the case to that of baseball's [[Danny Almonte]].{{cite news |last1=Bensinger |first1=Ken|last2=Stevens|first2=Matt||url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/sportsnow/la-sp-sn-shabazz-muhammad-20130322,0,1805254.story |title=Shabazz Muhammad's new age (20, not 19) could hurt draft status |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=March 22, 2013 |archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6H2LULcHk|archivedate=May 31, 2013|deadurl=no}} While Muhammad's father said the younger age in UCLA's media guide was "a mistake", numerous sources online show that Muhammad had been passing himself off as younger for years.{{cite video|title=PointguardU.com Shabazz Muhammad Interview from Las Vegas|time=0:41|publisher=pointguardu.com|publication-date=July 24, 2009|accessdate=May 31, 2013}} ==Awards/Honors== ===High school=== [[File:Shabazz Muhammad lean.jpg|thumb|upright|200px|Muhammad
